items.title: A spatial AI-based biomarker with independent prognostic value in early low- and intermediate- risk breast cancer
items.abstract: Background: Patients with ER-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer of low or intermediate grade are generally considered to have a favourable prognosis, yet a number will recur. This risk is poorly captured by standard clinicopathological factors. AI-based medical devices for whole slide image (WSI) analyses used for risk-stratification often predict on slide-level thereby overlooking spatial localisation of the biomarkers. We hypothesise that the spatial distribution of a previously reported AI-based marker provides independent prognostic value beyond its global score. Patients and Methods: This Swedish multicentre cohort study includes 6106 patients with primary invasive breast cancer: 3078 from the Stockholm region (training) and 3028 from Skane (independent test). Tile-level high-grade morphology scores were generated with ViT_DG, a vision-transformer adaptation of DeepGrade, and the presence of clusters of high-risk tiles localised at the invasive tumour front was defined as a binary biomarker. Primary analyses were pre-specified in the ER-positive/HER2-negative/lymph-node-negative and Grade 1-2 subgroup. Association with breast-cancer recurrence-free interval (BCRFI) and distant metastasis were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models (HR). Results: In the primary subgroup (n=1536 training; n=1403 test), tumour front clusters were present in 37% and 39% of patients. Cluster-positive status was associated with a 2.30-fold increased risk in the external test. Cluster-negative patients achieved a 10-year BCRFI of 95.3%, equivalent to Grade 1 patients and better than Grade 2 (92.4%), whereas cluster-positive patients (90.2%) did worse than the Grade 3 reference. The association was retained in patients classified as low-risk by ViT_DG (test set multivariable HR 2.86), identifying high-risk patients not captured by the global score. Conclusions: The absence of high-risk morphology clusters at the tumour front is an independent prognostic indicator, identifying a low-risk group independently of the global AI biomarker classification. More broadly, preserving the spatial distribution of AI-derived predictions enables prognostic stratification beyond slide-level aggregation.
items.authors: Boissin, C.; Xiang, Y.; Liu, B.; Vallon-Christersson, J.; Walker, E.; Hartman, J.; Rantalainen, M.

items.title: Advancing genetic pathogenicity prediction with three-dimensional proteoform-phenotype analysis
items.abstract: Ascertaining the pathogenicity and clinical relevance of genetic mutations is a longstanding challenge across human disease. This is particularly relevant for genes with many variants of unknown significance (VUS), such as PRPH2-retinopathy, where complex variable phenotype patterns and limited genotype correlations hinder application of precision-medicine therapies. Recent AI-based pathogenicity tools, while powerful, may be limited by insufficient mechanistic or phenotypic training data. We established a three-dimensional proteoform-phenotype analysis framework by combining AI-generated protein structural models with clinical genomics data, in which expert consensus adjudicates model outputs through a human-in-the-loop AI approach, to evaluate 46 curated pathogenic missense variants against a background VUS pool. The framework was prospectively validated using an independently evaluated clinical patient cohort. This analysis resolved spatial biophysical signatures corresponding to distinct clinical phenotypes (i.e., retinitis pigmentosa, macular dystrophy, and pattern dystrophy) as well as complex blended presentations. Leveraging these confirmed structural signatures, we prioritized high-risk VUS. This mechanism-resolved framework can be extended to other therapeutically actionable genes to identify novel causal variants and improve diagnosis, prognosis, and better select rare, eligible patients for emerging molecular gene therapy trials.
items.authors: Sun, Y. J.; Velez, G.; Li, A. S.; Kumar, A.; Vu, J. T.; Phillips, C. J.; Rasmussen, D. K.; Oh, J. K.; Costa, M. G. S.; Tsang, S. H.; Sun, Y.; Bassuk, A. G.; Mahajan, V. B.

items.title: Sex-aware Cross-tissue Regulatory Transformer Identified Sexually Dimorphic Alzheimer's Disease Risk Loci and Causal Cellular Circuit
items.abstract: Sex differences in Alzheimer's disease (AD) genetic effects and regulatory contexts remain incompletely resolved. We analyzed 449,335 European-ancestry participants using sex-stratified and genotype-by-sex models and developed STAGE-AD, a Transformer integrating molecular QTLs, epigenomic and single-cell annotations. Sex-stratified analyses identified eight female and three male genome-wide-significant signals provisionally classified as novel. Primary test-set area under the precision-recall curve was 0.895 (95% confidence interval, 0.877-0.912), decreasing to 0.751 under locus hold-out and 0.681 under APOE-region hold-out. Statistical-genetic integration in independent HUNT and MVP cohorts supported 236 genes at 106 loci. Prespecified lifetime-risk assumptions yielded liability-scale SNP heritabilities of 11.42% in females and 9.23% in males. Ablations indicated that female-biased predictions depended on glial annotations and male-biased predictions on endothelial and oligodendrocyte annotations. Eleven candidate variant-gene-tissue-cell-pathology chains were evaluated using multi-omics and neuropathological data from 579 NPAD brain donors. These findings underscore the importance of considering sex-specific genetic architectures in the study of health conditions, including Alzheimer's disease, paving the way for more targeted treatment strategies.
items.authors: Cheng, Z.; Judaprawira, S.; Perez, J.; Goldstein, A.

items.title: COMBINING CHEST X-RAY AND CLINICAL COVARIATES FOR OSTEOPOROSIS SCREENING: A MULTIMODAL DEEP LEARNING APPROACH
items.abstract: Osteoporosis is a major global health concern, yet screening remains inaccessible in many economically challenged and low-resource settings due to the high cost and operational complexity the gold standard, Dual-energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA) scan, requires. This study presents a multimodal deep-learning approach for opportunistic osteoporosis screening using chest X-rays and clinical variables such as age and gender. A total of 406 samples were retrospectively collected from a national hospital, comprising annotated chest radiographs paired with their DXA results from patients 50 and above. Two convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, ResNet50 and EfficientNetb3, were deployed under three configurations: image-only, early fusion, and late fusion. Image preprocessing includes CLAHE+Gamma Correction, followed by resizing, local regions of interest (ROI) extraction, and augmentation. The multimodal integration was conducted via early fusion (pixel-level) and late fusion (feature-level), with clinical variables normalized and encoded into a 1 x 3 vector. A custom Residual MLP classifier was employed in the late fusion models. Hyperparameter tuning was performed using Optuna's Bayesian optimization. Evaluation metrics included Accuracy, AUC, Precision, Recall, Sensitivity, and F1 Score. Among all models, Late Fusion EfficientNetb3 achieved the best performance on the global chest X-ray, with an AUC of 72.73%. Moreover, EfficientNetb3 consistently outperformed the ResNet50 architecture across all local ROI, Right Clavicle, Right Scapula, and Spine , with fusion models yielding higher sensitivity and balanced classification. The framework achieved competitive diagnostic performance despite the limitations of chest radiographs and an imbalanced dataset. Moreover, the findings demonstrated the feasibility of integrating chest X-rays with clinical covariates for AI-assisted osteoporosis screening, aiming to fill the accessibility gaps in preventive bone health diagnostics.
items.authors: kobayashi, v.; Baluyut, G.; Punsalan, J.

items.title: Epigenome Alterations and 3D Chromatin Architecture Remodeling in Inflammatory Macrophage Activation under Diabetic Conditions
items.abstract: Aberrant monocyte/macrophage activation in diabetes drives chronic inflammation and diabetic complications. Although epigenetic mechanisms are implicated in these processes, the contribution of three-dimensional (3D) chromatin reorganization remains unclear. Here, we use integrated multi-omics approaches to profile gene expression, chromatin accessibility and 3D chromatin architecture in human CD14 monocyte-derived macrophages exposed to high glucose and TNF- (HT), mimicking the diabetic milieu. HT induces inflammatory transcription programs that recapitulate those observed in diabetes and dynamically remodel chromatin accessibility, enhancer-promoter interactions, and topologically associated domains. Inflammatory genes exhibit increased chromatin accessibility, whereas cell cycle and metabolic genes display reduced accessibility and weakened enhancer-promoter interactions. These architectural changes promote the convergence of lineage-determining and signal-dependent transcription factors at enhancer-promoter loops, generating distinct regulatory hubs that orchestrate pro-inflammatory responses. Similar enhancer-promoter interactions are observed in peripheral blood derived monocytes from individuals with diabetes. Furthermore, perturbing chromatin interactions via CRISPR interference targeting HT-induced enhancers suppresses nearby CCL2 and other chemokine genes. Collectively, this first comprehensive enhancer connectome map of macrophages under diabetic conditions advances the field by revealing extensive disease-associated rewiring of the 3D epigenome, highlighting chromatin architecture and epigenetic mechanisms as potential therapeutic target for diabetes-associated inflammation.
items.authors: Reddy, M. A.; Bhattacharya, S.; Tanwar, V. S.; Malek, V.; Chen, Z.; Zhang, L.; Lanting, L.; Wu, X.; Grant, M. B.; Tompkins, J.; Chen, Z. B.; Natarajan, R.

items.title: Aldosterone mediates potassium-induced kidney fibrosis through tubular and mesenchymal mineralocorticoid receptor activation
items.abstract: Background Mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) activation drives chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression, as evidenced by the renoprotective effects of MR antagonists in clinical trials and conditional knockout models in myeloid and vascular smooth muscle cells. Dietary potassium stimulates aldosterone secretion, yet its impact on renal fibrosis, a hallmark of CKD progression, has not been systematically investigated. We hypothesised that high dietary potassium promotes renal fibrosis through aldosterone-driven MR activation, and sought to identify the renal cell populations mediating this effect. Methods Renal fibrosis was evaluated in two murine models: unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO, days 7-10) and inducible podocyte apoptosis (day 20), across dietary potassium concentrations ranging from 0.01% to 2%. GFR was measured by transcutaneous FITC-sinistrin clearance. Fibrosis was assessed by histology, immunofluorescence, and biochemistry. The MR dependence of the potassium effect was tested pharmacologically using finerenone and genetically using tissue-specific conditional knockout of MR in renal tubular epithelial and mesenchymal cells. Results High dietary potassium increased renal fibrosis in both models and reduced GFR by a further 50% in the podocyte apoptosis model. The pro-fibrotic effect persisted across sodium and anion variants, supporting specificity to potassium per se. Fibrosis burden correlated logarithmically with plasma aldosterone, and the pro-fibrotic effect of high potassium was attenuated by finerenone. Conditional MR deletion in tubular epithelial and mesenchymal cells independently recapitulated this protection, establishing cell-type specificity of the pathway. Conclusion High dietary potassium worsens renal fibrosis in murine models through aldosterone-dependent MR activation. This study provides the first in vivo genetic evidence that MR activation in renal tubular epithelial and mesenchymal cells can drive fibrosis, identifying a potentially actionable pathway in CKD management.
items.authors: CHARLEMAGNE, T.; SASSI, A.; Gjorgjieva, M.; yvon, r.; Tournier, M.; Fernandez, M.; Chassot, A.; Roth, I.; Veyrat-Durebex, C.; Ramakrishnan, S.; Rutkowski, J.; Feraille, E.; Olivier, V.

items.title: Evolutionarily conserved temperature dependency leads to loss of protein O-GlcNAc in mammalian hypothermia
items.abstract: O-N-acetylglucosaminylation (O-GlcNAcylation) is a non-canonical glycosylation of intracellular proteins suggested to be involved in diverse cellular processes, yet its regulation and specific effects on protein function remain elusive. The O-GlcNAc modification of protein serine and threonine residues is cycled by only two enzymes, O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) and O-GlcNAcase (OGA). O-GlcNAc sites lack a strict consensus sequence, suggesting that structural context rather than a defined motif governs the O-GlcNAc site selection. O-GlcNAcylation has been thought to be primarily regulated by the availability of its substrate, UDP-GlcNAc, produced by the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway (HBP). Here, we report a systemic loss of protein O-GlcNAc in Bcs1l mutant mice, a model of mitochondrial complex III deficiency. Although HBP precursor metabolites linked to mitochondrial function were decreased in the Bcs1l mutant liver, UDP-GlcNAc levels in the liver and other tissues were largely unaffected and did not correlate with the O-GlcNAc levels. Consistently, neither boosting UDP-GlcNAc with N-acetylglucosamine supplementation nor overexpression of the HBP rate-limiting enzyme GFPT1 restored O-GlcNAc levels, indicating that the loss was independent of the HBP. Instead, the body temperature of the hypothermic mutant mice showed a strong positive correlation with their O-GlcNAc level. Correcting body temperature via liver-targeted gene therapy, expression of alternative oxidase (AOX), or housing at 35oC prevented the loss of O-GlcNAc. Pharmacological inhibition of OGA restored O-GlcNAc levels in the hypothermic mice but did not affect disease progression, indicating that decreased O-GlcNAc is a physiologically normal consequence of hypothermia. We show that temperature dictates the O-GlcNAc status also across Drosophila species, zebrafish, and cultured mammalian cells. In cultured cells, hypothermia decreased OGT and increased OGA expression transcriptionally, indicating their ratio as a simple regulatory mechanism. Proteome solubility profiling revealed that O-GlcNAc alters the proteome structural and/or interactome landscape. Together, our findings identify temperature as an evolutionarily conserved master regulator of O-GlcNAcylation, which we propose protects the proteome from temperature-dependent fluctuations in both poikilothermic and homeothermic organisms.
items.authors: Upadhyay, D.; Kietz, C.; Sultana, N.; Banerjee, R.; Gaetani, M.; Kankare, M.; Fellman, V.; Purhonen, J.; Kallijarvi, J.
items.title_zh: 进化保守的温度依赖性导致哺乳动物低温下蛋白质O-GlcNAc丧失
items.summary_zh: O-N-乙酰氨基葡萄糖化（O-GlcNAcylation）是一种非典型的细胞内蛋白糖基化，参与多种细胞过程，但其调控机制及对蛋白功能的具体影响尚不明确。O-GlcNAc修饰由O-GlcNAc转移酶（OGT）和O-GlcNAcase（OGA）两种酶循环进行。O-GlcNAc位点缺乏严格的共识序列，表明结构背景而非特定基序决定O-GlcNAc位点选择。我们在Bcs1l突变小鼠（线粒体复合体III缺乏模型）中发现蛋白O-GlcNAc的系统性丧失。尽管与线粒体功能相关的HBP前体代谢物在Bcs1l突变肝脏中减少，但肝脏及其他组织中的UDP-GlcNAc水平基本不受影响，且与O-GlcNAc水平无关。补充N-乙酰氨基葡萄糖或过表达HBP限速酶GFPT1均未恢复O-GlcNAc水平，表明丧失与HBP无关。相反，低温突变小鼠的体温与其O-GlcNAc水平呈强正相关。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，哺乳动物在低温环境下，O-GlcNAc修饰的丧失与温度依赖性进化保守性有关，而非代谢物水平的变化。
items.l2_summary: O-N-乙酰氨基葡萄糖化（O-GlcNAcylation）是一种重要的细胞内蛋白糖基化修饰，参与多种细胞过程，但其调控机制及对蛋白功能的具体影响仍不明确。O-GlcNAc修饰的循环由O-GlcNAc转移酶（OGT）和O-GlcNAcase（OGA）两种酶共同完成。研究表明，O-GlcNAc位点缺乏严格的共识序列，这意味着其选择主要受结构背景的影响，而非特定的基序。通过对Bcs1l突变小鼠（线粒体复合体III缺乏模型）的研究，发现这些小鼠中蛋白O-GlcNAc的系统性丧失。尽管与线粒体功能相关的HBP前体代谢物在Bcs1l突变小鼠的肝脏中显著减少，但肝脏及其他组织中的UDP-GlcNAc水平基本保持不变，并且与O-GlcNAc水平无关。此外，补充N-乙酰氨基葡萄糖或过表达HBP限速酶GFPT1均未能恢复O-GlcNAc水平，进一步表明O-GlcNAc的丧失与HBP代谢途径无关。相反，研究发现低温突变小鼠的体温与其O-GlcNAc水平呈现出强正相关关系。这一发现提示，温度依赖性可能在哺乳动物的O-GlcNAc修饰中发挥重要作用，进而影响蛋白质的功能和细胞的生理状态。整体而言，这项研究揭示了低温对哺乳动物O-GlcNAc修饰的影响，强调了温度在调控蛋白质修饰中的潜在作用。

items.title: Decadal warming is linked to thermal tolerance and transcriptome reprogramming in a seagrass
items.abstract: Ocean warming and marine heatwaves threaten seagrasses, which are considered highly vulnerable to rising temperatures. We compared thermal stress responses of the tropical seagrass Halophila stipulacea collected from the Gulf of Aqaba in 2017 and 2022. Under mesocosm-applied thermal stress, 2017 plants showed reduced growth, impaired photochemistry, and extensive transcriptomic changes. In contrast, 2022 plants maintained normal growth and photochemistry with minimal transcriptional responses. The enhanced thermal stress tolerance of 2022 plants was associated with a 'stress-ready' transcriptome, with many stress-response genes already up/downregulated under control conditions, including those encoding heat, oxidative stress, and abscisic acid signaling proteins. These changes coincided with local ocean warming and a shift from episodic to chronic thermal stress. Our findings provide the first longitudinal dataset in a seagrass that tracks physiological and molecular changes occurring concurrently with documented ocean warming.
items.authors: Nguyen, H. M.; Lipkin, N. L.; Kaminer, M.; Winters, G.; Barak, S.

items.title: Powdery mildew fungi block plant vacuolar traffic to suppress immunity
items.abstract: Plant immunity can be activated by membrane-localized pattern recognition receptors or by cytosolic nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) receptors, while it can be counteracted by pathogen secreted effectors. Manifestation of immunity often involves endomembrane traffic. However, limited evidence is available for such an involvement in NLR-mediated immunity, which typically includes a hypersensitive reaction (HR)-programmed cell death response. Here we show that the barley powdery mildew fungus uses several effectors to target and inhibit the vacuolar trafficking pathway, which causes endomembrane markers to stall in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). We used this ER-stalling phenotype as a proxy to track fungal manipulation of the vacuolar pathway during different stages of the actual infection. Our data indicate that powdery mildew fungi interfere with the vacuolar pathway, but only temporarily, as the stalling is lifted once the fungal haustorial feeding structures are well-developed for nutrient uptake in epidermal cells. Notably, we show evidence that blocking the vacuolar pathway causes a general inhibition of NLR-mediated HR, and that this mechanism is taken advantage of by the pathogen. Finally, we provide an example that the fungus can secrete a different set of effectors at the haustorial stage that result in the re-opening of the vacuolar pathway by inhibiting the initial vacuolar traffic-suppressing effectors.
items.authors: Deb, S.; Placido, J. P. A.; Li, X.; Doukoudaki, P.; Sabelleck, B.; Velasquez-Zapata, V.; Fuerst, G.; Routya, B.; Elmore, J. M.; Christensen, A.; Wise, R. P.; Thordal-Christensen, H.
items.title_zh: 白粉病真菌通过抑制植物液泡运输来阻碍免疫反应
items.summary_zh: 植物免疫可通过膜定位的模式识别受体或细胞质中的核苷酸结合富 leucine重复（NLR）受体激活，但病原体分泌的效应子可以对其产生抑制作用。我们研究了大麦白粉病真菌如何利用多种效应子靶向并抑制液泡运输通路，导致内膜标记物在内质网（ER）中停滞。我们使用这种ER停滞表型作为追踪真菌在不同感染阶段对液泡通路操控的代理。数据表明，白粉病真菌干扰液泡通路，但这种干扰是暂时的，因为一旦真菌的吸器结构在表皮细胞中充分发育以进行营养吸收，停滞就会解除。值得注意的是，我们发现阻断液泡通路会普遍抑制NLR介导的超敏反应（HR），这一机制被病原体所利用。最后，我们提供了一个例子，表明真菌在吸器阶段可以分泌不同的效应子，从而通过抑制液泡通路的方式重新开启液泡通路。
items.l1_lead: 白粉病真菌通过暂时抑制植物液泡运输，干扰免疫反应，利用效应子在不同感染阶段操控植物的防御机制。
items.l2_summary:
研究表明，白粉病真菌通过抑制植物的液泡运输通路来阻碍植物的免疫反应。植物的免疫反应主要依赖于膜定位的模式识别受体和细胞质中的核苷酸结合富 leucine重复（NLR）受体的激活。然而，病原体分泌的效应子可以对这些受体产生抑制作用。我们对大麦白粉病真菌的研究显示，该真菌利用多种效应子靶向并抑制液泡运输通路，导致内膜标记物在内质网（ER）中停滞。我们将这种ER停滞表型作为追踪真菌在不同感染阶段对液泡通路操控的代理。

实验数据表明，白粉病真菌确实干扰了液泡通路，但这种干扰是暂时的。当真菌的吸器结构在表皮细胞中充分发育以进行营养吸收后，停滞现象会解除。值得注意的是，研究还发现，阻断液泡通路会普遍抑制NLR介导的超敏反应（HR），这一机制被病原体所利用。通过这些发现，我们可以看到，真菌在吸器阶段能够分泌不同的效应子，从而通过抑制液泡通路的方式重新开启液泡通路。这一研究为理解植物与病原体之间的相互作用提供了新的视角，揭示了病原体如何通过操控植物细胞内的运输机制来逃避植物的免疫监测。

items.title: Integrative Multi-omics Analysis of the Human Skeletal Muscle Response to Endurance or Resistance Exercise: Findings from the Molecular Transducers of Physical Activity Consortium (MoTrPAC)
items.abstract: The Molecular Transducers of Physical Activity Consortium (MoTrPAC) was established to systematically characterize the molecular basis of the health benefits of exercise. Here, we present the integrative, multi-omics response of human skeletal muscle to acute endurance (EE) and resistance (RE) exercise. Distinct temporal responses were observed, with changes in ATAC-seq, phosphoproteome, and metabolome occurring before changes in the transcriptome and proteome. These distinct temporal multi-omic dynamics were used to identify transcriptional regulatory hubs converging around MEF2A and NFIC regulation of autophagy, angiogenesis and metabolism. Further, early RE-specific phosphoproteome signatures counteracted epigenetic modifications and downregulated transcripts involved in protein turnover. Additional findings include suppression of HIPK2/3 kinase signatures linked to the acute exercise regulation of sarcomeric proteins TTN, NEB, ANKRD2 and LMOD2. Our data demonstrate distinct temporal regulation across the multi-omic landscape of human skeletal muscle, with EE and RE eliciting common and unique molecular signatures.

items.title: AXIS: Agentic Extraction and Integration of Simulation Scenarios for Quantitative Systems Pharmacology
items.abstract: Quantitative Systems Pharmacology (QSP) models are executable and mechanistic representations of biological systems that are increasingly used to design, evaluate, and help enrich clinical trials. Reusing a published model, however, requires knowing what each entity represents biologically (often inferable only from its relations to other entities) and what value it must take for a given scenario, information carried in the accompanying publication, not the model file. Agentic systems automate simulation setup from user-specified tasks over standardized parameter sets. In parallel, literature-mining tools extract reported quantities from publications. However, closing the loop, going from paper and model to an executable configuration that reproduces the published result, remains a manual curation task. Here, we present AXIS, a modular multi-agent framework that converts a published QSP model together with its companion publication into simulation-ready configurations. The framework integrates dependency-aware entity grounding, evidence-linked scenario extraction, semantic and structural entity search, sandboxed deterministic computation, and expert input on ambiguity. AXIS comprises three modules that ground the model's entities, recover the scenarios described in the paper, and resolve each into concrete parameter assignments. We demonstrate the framework end-to-end on a published disease model, reconstructing the figure reported in its companion publication. AXIS recovers the reported scenarios, produces parameter assignments matching an expert-curated ground truth, and defers to an expert where a required quantity appears in neither source.
items.authors: Kazemeini, A.; Prieto, J.; Balaji Kuttae, S.; Siokis, A.; Gallagher, C.; Klabunde, T.; Singh, G.; Andreani, T.; Passban, P.

items.title: Spontaneous slow waves index multiple dimensions of recovery in Disorders of Consciousness
items.abstract: Whether and how residual awareness is expressed in patients with Disorders of Consciousness (DoC) depends on the severity of brain damage and the transient functional state of the cortex at assessment. Classically, DoC are associated with electroencephalographic (EEG) slowing, marked by high-amplitude slow waves, even during the day. Yet, slow waves are also a hallmark of healthy sleep, where they are thought to serve restorative functions and to help maintain network homeostasis. Here, we asked whether slow waves in DoC can provide insights into the severity of cortical dysfunction or, conversely, into the preservation of residual awareness and recovery potential, by characterizing their spatial, temporal and morphological properties. We analyzed 256-channel EEG recorded during the Local-Global auditory paradigm in 236 DoC patients, including 123 in Unresponsive Wakefulness Syndrome (UWS), 62 in a Minimally Conscious State minus (MCS-) and 29 in MCS plus (MCS+). High-amplitude slow waves were detected as local events, and their density, amplitude and slopes were quantified scalp-wide and channel-wise, by mean level and temporal variability across the recording. Slow-wave features were related to concurrent (Coma Recovery Scale-Revised - CRS-R, Local-Global paradigm) and follow-up (one-year Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended - GOS-E) assessments of consciousness and functional recovery. Associations with MRI-derived measures of cortical integrity and structural connectivity, and differences between anoxic and traumatic etiologies, were also examined. Slow waves were more frequent in less severe DoC patients (i.e., MCS) compared to UWS. Slow-wave slopes were also steeper frontally and increased at a faster rate in patients exhibiting higher levels of consciousness and/or markers of conscious access during the Local-Global paradigm. More frequent and steeper slow waves at baseline further predicted recovery of consciousness and of functional independence at one year. At the individual level, slow-wave features classified states of consciousness above chance (AUC = 0.62 and 0.71 for MCS- and MCS+ versus UWS), whereas outcome prediction remained modest (0.56-0.58). These clinical associations had a structural basis: slow-wave occurrence was greater after traumatic than anoxic injury and scaled with the integrity of subcortico-cortical projection fibers and consciousness-related cortical networks. Contrary to the classical view of delta activity as a non-specific marker of impaired consciousness, prominent spontaneous slow waves indexed behavioral and neurophysiological signs of awareness and better recovery. Beyond reflecting a propensity for pathological bistability, they may also signal the integrity of the networks required to generate them, together with their residual capacity for dynamic regulation.
items.authors: Ruyant Belabbas, A.; Boullet, A.; Manasova, D.; Le Coz, A.; Valente, M.; Lejeune, F.-X.; Sitt, J. D.; Naccache, L.; Rohaut, B.; Andrillon, T.
items.title_zh: 自发慢波反映意识障碍患者恢复的多维度指标
items.summary_zh: 意识障碍（DoC）患者的残余意识表现取决于脑损伤的严重程度及评估时皮层的瞬时功能状态。传统上，DoC与脑电图（EEG）慢波活动相关，表现为高幅慢波，即使在白天也明显存在。然而，慢波也是健康睡眠的标志，具有恢复功能并帮助维持网络稳态。本研究分析了236名DoC患者（包括123名无反应觉醒综合症（UWS）、62名最小意识状态减（MCS-）和29名最小意识状态增（MCS+））在局部-全局听觉范式下记录的256通道EEG。我们检测到高幅慢波作为局部事件，并量化了其在头皮上的密度、幅度和斜率。慢波特征与同时（昏迷恢复量表修订版 - CRS-R，局部-全局范式）和后续（一年格拉斯哥结果量表扩展版 - GOS-E）意识及功能恢复评估相关。
items.l1_lead: 本研究发现，自发高幅慢波活动可作为意识障碍患者恢复的多维度指标，与其意识和功能恢复评估密切相关。
items.l2_summary: 意识障碍（DoC）患者的残余意识水平与脑损伤的严重程度及评估时皮层的瞬时功能状态密切相关。传统上，DoC与脑电图（EEG）中的慢波活动相关，尤其是高幅慢波，即使在白天也显著存在。然而，慢波不仅是意识障碍的标志，也是健康睡眠的特征，具有恢复功能并帮助维持神经网络的稳态。本研究对236名DoC患者进行了分析，其中包括123名无反应觉醒综合症（UWS）、62名最小意识状态减（MCS-）和29名最小意识状态增（MCS+）患者，采用256通道EEG在局部-全局听觉范式下记录数据。研究中检测到的高幅慢波作为局部事件，其在头皮上的密度、幅度和斜率被量化。结果显示，慢波特征与同时的意识及功能恢复评估（使用昏迷恢复量表修订版 - CRS-R）以及后续的一年格拉斯哥结果量表扩展版（GOS-E）评估之间存在显著相关性。这一发现表明，高幅慢波不仅是评估DoC患者意识状态的重要指标，也可能反映其恢复潜力，为临床评估和干预提供了新的多维度指标。

items.title: Task demands shift motor learning from adaptation to feedback control in an unconstrained bimanual task
items.abstract: Bimanual actions are common in daily life, yet how task demands shape reliance on learning and control mechanisms remains largely unknown. We examined this in 73 participants who lifted a plate in virtual reality while we distorted visual motion of their right hand. During right-hand-only lifting, aftereffects were present but incomplete. Bimanual lifting with the same right-hand perturbation shifted learning further from adaptation toward feedback control: participants developed compensatory hand adjustments and showed smaller aftereffects. Relaxing precision demands improved success but neither restored aftereffects nor reduced compensation. Removing interlimb conflict by perturbing both hands did not improve success but eased compensatory adjustments and restored plate aftereffects to unimanual levels. Success rate during learning did not correlate with aftereffects, but faster movement speed did. This demonstrates that precision demands and interlimb conflict independently shift learning strategy in bimanual contexts.
items.authors: Varghese, R.; Rossi, C.; Malone, L. A.; Bastian, A. J.

items.title: Hippocampal extracellular matrix remodeling and temporally distinct glial reorganization following peripheral injury
items.abstract: Chronic pain is frequently accompanied by anxiety and other affective disturbances, but the molecular and cellular changes linking peripheral injury to persistent alterations in brain function remain incompletely defined. The hippocampal extracellular matrix (ECM) regulates synaptic plasticity, cellular signaling, and neuroimmune interactions and may therefore contribute to pain-related central plasticity. We used a tibial fracture/cast immobilization model to examine temporal changes in hippocampal ECM, glial morphology, and affective behavior following peripheral injury. Behavioral testing was performed at 3, 7, and 20 weeks after injury, while high-dimensional morphometric analysis of microglia and astrocytes was performed at 1, 3, 7, and 20 weeks. Hippocampal ECM associated molecular signals were mapped at the chronic stage using decellularization coupled with MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry imaging. Injured mice developed mechanical hypersensitivity and reduced exploration in two anxiety related paradigms during the early and chronic stages, with these behavioral phenotypes no longer detected at 20 weeks. At 7 weeks, injury was associated with changes in hippocampal ECM-associated peptide signals, including reduced signals corresponding to four ECM-associated proteins. Microglia and astrocytes exhibited distinct, time-dependent changes in density and multidimensional morphology, with some alterations persisting after behavioral measures returned toward control levels. In vitro, BV2 microglia exhibited rigidity-dependent changes in morphology, phagocytic behavior, and calcium signaling. Together, these findings define a temporally evolving hippocampal ECM and glial phenotype following peripheral injury and identify matrix biomechanics as a candidate regulator of microglial function.
items.authors: Ge, C.; Kausar, V.; Xu, L.; Maghsoudi, A.; Shtudland, G.; Amrami, M.; Betancourt, M.; Niaz, A.; Zirkiyev, J.; Alvarado, S. G.; Abzalimov, R.; He, Y.; Tajerian, M.

items.title: Immediate cortical responses to transcranial magnetic stimulation of the human motor leg area
items.abstract: Background: Immediate transcranial evoked potentials (iTEPs) are ultra-early electroencephalographic responses elicited by single-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) of the primary motor cortical hand area (M1-HAND). Their characteristic latency, waveform, and sensitivity to short-interval intracortical inhibition suggest a close relationship to the cortical generators of indirect corticospinal volleys (I-waves). Here, we tested the hypothesis that iTEPs constitute a fundamental physiological response of human motor cortex and therefore generalize across motor representations, including the leg representation (M1-LEG). Methods: Single-pulse TMS was delivered over the motor cortical representation of the right tibialis anterior (TA) in 16 healthy volunteers. In a subset of participants (n=10), stimulus-response curves and paired-pulse short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI) measures were obtained. Results: TMS of M1-LEG elicited reproducible iTEPs consisting of a slow positive deflection with superimposed high-frequency peaks with topographic maxima in electrodes adjacent to the stimulation site. M1-LEG iTEPs emerged close to active motor threshold and increased in prevalence and amplitude with increasing stimulation intensity. Paired-pulse stimulation produced consistent SICI of the second and third iTEP peaks. M1-LEG stimulation also evoked conventional later TEPs with latencies and polarities closely resembling those recorded after M1-HAND stimulation. Conclusions: TMS of the human M1-LEG elicits robust iTEPs that closely resemble those recorded from M1-HAND in their timing, intensity dependence, and sensitivity to intracortical inhibition. These findings indicate that iTEPs are not specific to M1-HAND but reflect a general physiological response of human motor cortex closely linked to corticospinal I-wave generation. This broadens their utility as a non-invasive probe of excitatory and inhibitory circuit dynamics throughout the human motor system.
items.authors: Beck, M. M.; Nuyts, M.; Sakalauskaite, L.; Rothwell, J.; Siebner, H. R.; Christiansen, L.

items.title: Aging reshapes odor-evoked dynamics in central olfactory circuits
items.abstract: Olfactory decline is among the earliest signs of aging and predicts later cognitive decline and neurodegenerative disease. Age-related impairments in odor identification and discrimination implicate central olfactory brain regions in both mice and humans, but it remains unclear where in the processing hierarchy aging alters neural function relating to these cognitive and perceptual deficits. To resolve this, we acquired simultaneous Neuropixels recordings from olfactory bulb (OB) and piriform cortex (PCx) in young and old mice during awake, head-fixed odor presentation, allowing us to probe multiple levels of odor response features within each animal. Our recordings revealed a shift toward greater excitation in both regions and reduced inhibitory neuron activity in PCx. Aging also restructured odor-evoked local field potential (LFP) oscillations within and across regions, with strongly elevated beta power and coherence. Population odor representations were less discriminable in OB, but not in PCx. Thus, our results point to reduced discriminability of OB population odor representations as the clearest neural analog of previously reported discrimination deficits. Single-unit, LFP, and population measures did not collapse onto a single axis using dimensionality reduction, indicating that several partly independent processes reshape the dynamics of odor responses in central olfactory circuits with aging. Together, these findings identify central circuit excitation/inhibition (E/I) and oscillatory imbalances that parallel age-related olfactory dysfunction despite largely preserved odor responsivity.
items.authors: Chapman, I. F.; Bolding, K. A.

items.title: Model-based pupil deconvolution reveals latent attentional dynamics
items.abstract: Changes in pupil size have been widely used as an indirect measure of attention. However, attention engages on a faster timescale than the pupillary response. Therefore, the slow time course of the pupil response makes it difficult to distinguish attentional responses to stimuli presented in close temporal succession. Although signal deconvolution has been used in previous research to estimate latent attentional responses from the pupil signal, existing methods primarily model dilation without considering the visual stimulus evoked constriction phase of the pupil. Here, we introduce a dual-kernel deconvolution model that models constriction and dilation using separate impulse response functions. Using an RSVP paradigm with emotional faces as target stimuli, we demonstrate that the proposed model estimates latent attentional response despite substantial overlap in the measured pupil signal. Importantly, the recovered attentional response resembles the time course of attentional allocation previously predicted by several models of Attentional Blink. Together, these findings demonstrate that the dynamics of latent attentional episodes can be recovered from the pupil response with a temporal resolution previously obscured by the sluggishness of the pupillary response. The proposed method is also provided as a usable software package that serves as a general tool for investigating the temporal dynamics of attention in rapid visual paradigms.
items.authors: Maity, S.; Mathot, S.; Ray, S. B.

items.title: Eyes on the prize: a neural basis of perceptual choking under pressure
items.abstract: Even professional athletes sometimes fail to perform when it matters most. This phenomenon, known as choking under pressure, has been observed in a variety of motor and cognitive tasks. Can inordinately large rewards influence even sensory processing, and if so, what might be its neural basis? To probe this, we studied rhesus monkeys performing a challenging color change detection task and recorded from populations of neurons in visual area V4. We found that monkeys underperformed when offered rare "jackpot" rewards and uncovered associated detrimental alterations in V4 population activity. These findings were consistent with misallocated spatial attention, providing a potential neural basis for perceptual choking under pressure.
items.authors: McDonnell, M. E.; Chandrasekaran, A. N.; Ki, C. S.; Smoulder, A. L.; Miyata, H.; Yu, B.; Batista, A. P.; Smith, M. A.; Chase, S. M.

items.title: Biophysical modeling of excitation/inhibition imbalance in Alzheimer's disease
items.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Alzheimer's disease (AD) involves early sensory and perceptual changes that can precede memory decline. We developed a two-layer rate-based neural model of early and higher visual areas with feedforward, feedback, and recurrent connections to examine how excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance shapes visual motion perception in AD. METHODS: Using Motion-Induced Position Shift and Altered Motion Repulsion stimuli, we factorially manipulated excitatory (E) and inhibitory (I) subfield power and connectivity to examine their effects on illusion representation across visual layers. RESULTS: Increased E, decreased I, and increased E/I reduced illusion representation, consistent with reduced illusion susceptibility in AD, whereas the converse increased illusion representation, reflecting neurotypical processing. Higher-level layer 2 representations were more resistant to E/I perturbations than lower-level layer 1. Illusion representation was less affected by E/I increases in intra-areal (recurrent) connectivity than in inter-areal (feedforward/feedback) connectivity. DISCUSSION: This mechanistic framework links E/I balance and connectivity to altered visual motion illusion representations in AD and suggests that E/I and connectivity measures may provide probes of early AD neurobiology. The framework may also generalize beyond vision.
items.authors: Deng, Q.; Chen, C.; Zikopoulos, B.; Yazdanbakhsh, A.

items.title: Retinotopic organization of head-orienting vectors in the pigeon ventral lateral geniculate nucleus
items.abstract: The ventral lateral geniculate nucleus (GLv) is a conserved retinorecipient structure positioned between visual and premotor systems, yet its role in visuomotor transformations remains poorly understood. Here, we examined whether the pigeon GLv contains a spatially organized motor representation linking visual-field locations to orienting movements. Anatomical tracing identified descending projections from neurons in the GLv inner lamina (GLv-li) through pretectal and tegmental regions toward pontine targets. GLv-li projection neurons are GABAergic, yet electrical microstimulation of GLv-li in awake pigeons evoked rapid head movements followed by smaller eye movements. Each stimulation locus produced a reproducible characteristic motor vector whose direction and duration were largely insensitive to stimulation parameters, whereas movement amplitude and velocity approached site-specific plateaus. Movements initiated from different head positions were better explained by repetition of a fixed displacement than by convergence toward a common spatial goal. Critically, motor-vector direction was systematically related to the direction of the visual receptive field represented at the same GLv locus, while motor-vector amplitude covaried with receptive-field eccentricity. These defining features persisted after optic tectum ablation. Together, these findings reveal a retinotopically-organized map of fixed-vector head movements in the avian GLv and identify a tectum-independent route through which visual spatial representations can access descending orienting circuitry.
items.authors: Severin, D.; Reynaert, B.; Vega-Zuniga, T.; Letelier, J. C.; Marin, G.; Karten, H. J.; Mpodozis, J.

items.title: Focal drug uncaging for the precise control of endogenous nicotinic receptors in behaving mice
items.abstract: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptors shape diverse brain functions, including reward, aversion, and pain, but dissecting their roles in vivo requires drug delivery with spatiotemporal precision that conventional pharmacology cannot provide. Here we establish in vivo photopharmacology of endogenous nicotinic receptors: two complementary, highly-potent agonists, administered systemically in an inactive caged form, are photoreleased locally in target brain circuits of behaving wild-type mice. Despite irreversible photochemistry, photoactivation can be repeated over many trials on a minute timescale, for hours following a single injection. Local uncaging evokes circuit-specific dopamine release, drives place preference from the ventral tegmental area and aversion from the interpeduncular nucleus, and, in pain circuits, reveals a pronociceptive effect masked when the same agonists are given systemically. By controlling where and when nicotinic signaling acts, this approach exposes circuit-specific drug effects invisible to conventional pharmacology, and outlines a general strategy for on-demand control of endogenous receptors in vivo.
items.authors: Guyon, N.; Mohayyaei, M.; Bergel, A.; Grellier, G.; Jehl, J.; Pietrancosta, N.; Rebola, N.; Francois, A.; Faure, P.; Ellis-Davies, G. C. R.; Mourot, A.

items.title: Synaptic density imaging associates with performance but not self-report in autism
items.abstract: Autism is a common neurodevelopmental condition with considerable between-person variability and unknown biological etiology. Diagnosis of autism in adults relies on measurement of performance (e.g., clinician rating of social behavior, standardized assessment of cognition) and self-report of autism features. Our prior work revealed a strong relationship between clinician ratings of social function in autism and in vivo measures of synaptic density as measured by [11C]UCB-J PET (Matuskey et al., 2025). However, it is not understood how the measured aspects of the autism phenotype index underlying biology. Here, in a sample of 12 autistic adults, we address this question by relating synaptic density imaging to a range of performance measures, such as cognition and face recognition, in contrast to self-report measures. Our results identify a dissociation between these measurement types in that synaptic density correlates strongly with measures of performance but shows virtually no relationship with self-report. These findings suggest that, while self-report and performance measures share variance in characterizing phenotypes in autism, they diverge when mapping onto the underlying biology. Results suggest that higher synaptic density may index a general mechanism that facilitates social and cognitive performance across a range of tasks. These data also indicate that performance and self-report measures are not interchangeable in capturing brain-behavior correspondences in autism, a finding that can guide measure selection in future biomarker studies and clinical research.
items.authors: Naples, A. J.; Cayir, S.; Cukar-Capizzi, C.; Wolf, J. M.; Mcclelland, J. E.; Robertson, E. C.; Sawant, S. S.; Matuskey, D.; McPartland, J. C.
items.title_zh: 自闭症中突触密度成像与表现相关但与自我报告无关
items.summary_zh: 自闭症是一种常见的神经发育障碍，个体间差异显著且生物学病因尚不明确。成人自闭症的诊断依赖于表现测量（如临床社交行为评分、标准化认知评估）和自我报告特征。我们之前的研究发现，自闭症社交功能的临床评分与通过[11C]UCB-J PET测量的体内突触密度之间存在强相关。然而，如何将自闭症表型的测量与生物学基础联系起来尚不清楚。在12名自闭症成人样本中，我们将突触密度成像与认知和面孔识别等表现测量进行关联，发现突触密度与表现测量强相关，但与自我报告几乎没有关系。这些结果表明，自我报告和表现测量在表征自闭症表型时存在共同变异，但在映射到生物学基础时则出现分歧。结果提示，较高的突触密度可能指示一种促进社交和认知表现的普遍机制。
items.l1_lead: 自闭症的突触密度与表现测量存在强相关性，但与自我报告几乎无关，提示生物学基础与表型测量之间的差异。
items.l2_summary: 自闭症是一种常见的神经发育障碍，其个体差异显著且生物学病因尚不明确。成人自闭症的诊断通常依赖于表现测量，如临床社交行为评分和标准化认知评估，以及自我报告特征。我们之前的研究表明，自闭症社交功能的临床评分与通过[11C]UCB-J PET（正电子发射断层扫描）测量的体内突触密度之间存在强相关性。然而，如何将自闭症表型的测量与其生物学基础联系起来仍然不清楚。在本研究中，我们对12名自闭症成人样本进行了突触密度成像与认知和面孔识别等表现测量的关联分析，结果显示突触密度与表现测量之间存在强相关性，但与自我报告几乎没有关系。这一发现表明，自我报告和表现测量在表征自闭症表型时存在共同变异，但在映射到生物学基础时却出现了分歧。这些结果提示，较高的突触密度可能指示一种促进社交和认知表现的普遍机制，强调了在理解自闭症时，生物学指标与行为表现之间的复杂关系。通过这种研究，我们能够更深入地探讨自闭症的生物学基础，为未来的诊断和干预提供新的视角。

items.title: Impaired astrocytic Cx43 syncytial network in lateral habenula affects synaptic connectivity and drives adolescent stress-induced depression
items.abstract: Adolescent depression is a major neuropsychiatric disorder induced by early life stress; the underlying cellular mechanisms instigating pathological circuit malformation remain unclear, and, consequently, effective therapeutic strategy is limited. Here, we analysed the contribution of astrocytes to early life stress-induced adolescent depression using a mouse model of parental separation. We identified a previously unrecognised regional specialisation of lateral habenula (LHb) astrocytes, characterised by compact cellular domains, abundant leaflets, and enhanced Cx43 gap junctional coupling. Parental separation selectively reduced astrocytic Cx43 expression and gap junctional communication in the LHb, which was accompanied by profound astrocytic atrophy and loss of leaflets. Single-cell sequencing further revealed that parental separation induces a broad reorganisation of LHb astrocyte transcriptional states, including metabolic, stress-response, and inflammatory programs; moreover, it specifically reduces astrocyte-neuron communication. Consistent with this, we found that structural remodelling of LHb astrocytes affected tripartite synapse geometry, resulting in impaired excitatory and inhibitory synaptic transmission, and neuronal Ca2+ hyperexcitability, all ultimately associated with depressive-like behaviours. Selective knockdown of astrocytic Cx43 in the LHb recapitulated these pathological changes and translated into depressive-like behaviours. Mechanistically, we found that impaired Cx43 gap junctional communication is associated with excessive astrocytic Ca2+ dynamics, resulting in Rac1-GTPase activation and decreased p-Ezrin levels. In vivo inhibition of LHb astrocytic Ca2+ signalling rescued astrocytic atrophy and depressive-like behaviours following parental separation. Together, our findings establish a Cx43-Ca2+-Rac1-p-Ezrin pathway that links gap junction malfunction to structural remodelling of astrocytes and disruption of neuron-astrocyte interactions in the developing LHb. Our study reveals astrocytic Ca2+ dysregulation as an active downstream effector of Cx43 dysfunction and identifies a regionally specialised astrocytic mechanism through which early-life stress disrupts synaptic transmission and neuronal function during adolescence, providing a potential cellular target for intervention in adolescent depression.
items.authors: Li, H.; Wang, Q.; Su, Y.; Chen, H.; Wu, Z.; Chen, X.; Wang, C.; Zhao, Y.; Li, D.; Huang, X.; Fu, R.; Huang, W.; Tang, Y.; Niu, J.; Verkhratsky, A.; Yi, C.
items.title_zh: 侧脑室星形胶质细胞Cx43网络受损影响突触连接与青春期抑郁
items.summary_zh: 青春期抑郁是由早期生活压力引发的主要神经精神疾病，其病理电路形成的细胞机制尚不清楚。本文利用小鼠父母分离模型分析了星形胶质细胞在早期生活压力诱导的青春期抑郁中的作用。我们发现侧脑室（LHb）星形胶质细胞具有紧凑的细胞域、丰富的叶片和增强的Cx43间隙连接特征。父母分离选择性降低了LHb中星形胶质细胞的Cx43表达和间隙连接通信，伴随显著的星形胶质细胞萎缩和叶片丧失。单细胞测序进一步揭示，父母分离引起LHb星形胶质细胞转录状态的广泛重组，特别减少了星形胶质细胞与神经元的通信。这种结构重塑影响了三元突触几何形状，导致兴奋性和抑制性突触传递受损，神经元Ca2+过度兴奋，最终与抑郁样行为相关。
items.l1_lead: 侧脑室星形胶质细胞Cx43网络受损导致突触连接异常，进而影响青春期抑郁的发生与发展。
items.l2_summary:
青春期抑郁是一种主要由早期生活压力引发的神经精神疾病，其病理电路形成的细胞机制尚不明确。本文通过小鼠父母分离模型，探讨了星形胶质细胞在早期生活压力诱导的青春期抑郁中的作用。研究发现，侧脑室（LHb）中的星形胶质细胞具有紧凑的细胞域、丰富的叶片和增强的Cx43（连接蛋白43）间隙连接特征。然而，父母分离处理显著降低了LHb中星形胶质细胞的Cx43表达及其间隙连接通信，同时伴随出现了星形胶质细胞的萎缩和叶片的丧失。

通过单细胞测序，研究进一步揭示了父母分离对LHb星形胶质细胞转录状态的广泛重组，尤其是星形胶质细胞与神经元之间的通信显著减少。这种结构上的重塑影响了三元突触的几何形状，导致兴奋性和抑制性突触传递的受损，进而引发神经元内钙离子（Ca2+）的过度兴奋。这一系列变化最终与抑郁样行为密切相关，表明LHb星形胶质细胞的Cx43网络受损在青春期抑郁的发病机制中可能起着重要作用。研究结果为理解青春期抑郁的细胞机制提供了新的视角，并为未来的干预策略奠定了基础。

items.title: Design and Test Novel EEG Electrode Attachments for Type 4 Afro-textured Hairstyles
items.abstract: Black participants remain underrepresented in electroencephalography (EEG) research, partly because current EEG devices work poorly with dense, coily Type 4 Afro-textured hair. Research-grade EEG typically wires electrodes on a cap, and therefore the electrodes often fail to reach the scalp through dense, Afro-textured hair. Protocols that ask Black participants to unbraid or restyle protective hairstyles add burdens that discourage enrollment in research studies. To address this, we designed and tested 3D-printed attachments that fit onto an EEG electrode and anchored it directly in the hair, using the hairstyle itself as the mounting structure. We fabricated three design configurations for natural Afro-textured hair, cornrows/braids, and twists/microlocs. Seventeen healthy adults with Type 4a-4c hair used electrode attachments that matched their hairstyle. During a single visit, EEG was recorded with 16 conventional cap electrodes defined by the international 10-20 system and with 16 electrodes using novel electrode attachments anchored directly to their hair. Participants completed resting and walking trials with each system. Electrode-to-scalp distance and gel volume were measured during setup. Electrode disconnection, impedance, signal quality (i.e. peak alpha power and aperiodic (1/f) component), and comfort level were measured throughout the data collection. Compared with the conventional cap, the novel attachments reduced electrode-to-scalp distance, gel use, and impedance. Twenty percent of the conventional cap electrodes failed to connect to the scalp compared with 0.1% of novel electrodes. Impedance rose across trials for the conventional cap, whereas the novel attachments showed a smaller increase and maintained lower impedance throughout. Signal quality was significantly better using the novel attachments, while comfort level did not differ between systems. In conclusion, hair-anchored electrode attachment may present a feasible alternative to conventional cap-based EEG for people with Type 4 hair, yielding more usable channels and better signal quality, and supporting more inclusive EEG acquisition.
items.authors: Broor, M.; Ogunniyi, K.; Williamson, L.; Liu, C.

items.title: Dorsomedial striatal Bmal1 deletion in medium spiny neurons alters EPSCs and dendritic morphology after chronic exposure to alcohol in female mice.
items.abstract: Circadian clock genes in the striatum modulate alcohol drinking behavior in female mice, but the underlying synaptic mechanisms remain unknown. Medium spiny neurons (MSNs) of the striatum express D1- or D2-type dopamine receptors, which are differentially modulated by alcohol. Here we used whole-cell patch-clamp recordings to examine how deletion of the clock gene Bmal1 affects spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic currents (sEPSCs) in electrophysiologically identified D1 and D2 neurons of the female mouse dorsomedial striatum (DMS). Prior intermittent access to alcohol increased sEPSC amplitude in putative D1 neurons of wildtype mice without affecting sEPSC frequency, and this increase was accompanied by greater dendritic branching and complexity in biocytin-filled D1 MSNs. Bmal1 knockout had the opposite effect in D1 neurons, reducing sEPSC amplitude in both alcohol-exposed and alcohol-naive animals. In D2 neurons, alcohol produced only a non-significant trend toward increased sEPSC amplitude in wildtype mice, but a significant increase in Bmal1 knockout mice. Thus, local disruption of Bmal1 appears to block the alcohol-induced enhancement of sEPSCs in D1 neurons while unmasking a similar enhancement in D2 neurons. These findings may help explain how Bmal1 deletion in the DMS reduces alcohol consumption in female mice.
items.authors: Darvishmolla, M.; Courtemanche, R.; Amir, S.; Chapman, A.
items.title_zh: 去除雌性小鼠背内侧纹状体Bmal1基因影响酒精暴露后的突触传递
items.summary_zh: 本研究探讨了背内侧纹状体（DMS）中中型棘突神经元（MSNs）内生物钟基因Bmal1的缺失如何影响雌性小鼠在慢性酒精暴露后的自发性兴奋性突触后电流（sEPSCs）。采用全细胞膜片钳技术记录，发现间歇性接触酒精增加了野生型小鼠D1神经元的sEPSC幅度，而未影响频率，伴随树突分支和复杂性的增加。Bmal1基因敲除则在D1神经元中产生相反效果，降低了酒精暴露和未暴露动物的sEPSC幅度。D2神经元中，酒精对野生型小鼠的sEPSC幅度仅有非显著趋势，而在Bmal1敲除小鼠中则显著增加。因此，Bmal1的局部缺失似乎阻止了D1神经元中酒精诱导的sEPSC增强，同时揭示了D2神经元的类似增强。这些发现可能有助于解释Bmal1缺失如何减少雌性小鼠的酒精摄入。
items.l1_lead: 本研究发现，背内侧纹状体中Bmal1基因缺失会降低雌性小鼠在酒精暴露后的突触传递，可能影响其酒精摄入行为。
items.l2_summary:
本研究旨在探讨雌性小鼠背内侧纹状体（DMS）中中型棘突神经元（MSNs）内生物钟基因Bmal1的缺失对酒精暴露后自发性兴奋性突触后电流（sEPSCs）的影响。研究采用全细胞膜片钳技术进行记录，结果显示，间歇性接触酒精显著增加了野生型小鼠D1神经元的sEPSC幅度，而频率未受到影响，且伴随树突分支和复杂性的增加。这表明酒精暴露能够增强D1神经元的突触传递能力。然而，在Bmal1基因敲除小鼠中，D1神经元的sEPSC幅度却显著降低，无论是在酒精暴露还是未暴露的情况下，显示出Bmal1缺失对D1神经元的负面影响。

在D2神经元中，酒精对野生型小鼠的sEPSC幅度仅表现出非显著的趋势，而在Bmal1敲除小鼠中，sEPSC幅度则显著增加。这一结果表明，Bmal1的局部缺失似乎阻止了D1神经元中酒精诱导的sEPSC增强，同时在D2神经元中却出现了相反的增强效应。这些发现为理解Bmal1缺失如何影响雌性小鼠的酒精摄入提供了新的视角，可能揭示了生物钟基因在酒精相关行为中的重要作用。通过这些实验结果，研究为进一步探讨Bmal1基因在酒精依赖及相关神经机制中的作用奠定了基础。

items.title: Cross-Tissue Inflammatory Convergence Supports a Putative Muscle-Brain Axis in Alzheimer's Disease
items.abstract: Background Reduced muscle strength is associated with cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease (AD), suggesting that skeletal-muscle aging and AD-related neurodegeneration may share biological mechanisms. Vascular dysfunction, immune activation, and extracellular-matrix remodeling have been implicated in both tissues, but the extent of shared cellular and molecular programs remains unclear. We investigated cross-tissue transcriptional programs in aging skeletal muscle and AD-related brain tissue and evaluated whether related signals are detectable in peripheral blood. Methods We analyzed independent, unpaired human transcriptomic datasets from skeletal muscle (23 donors), the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus atlas (84 donors), and peripheral blood. Donor-aware models identified age-associated changes in muscle and transcriptomic changes across continuous pseudoprogression score (CPS) in brain. Cross-tissue comparisons focused on 30 brain donors within an early CPS window. Shared tissue-derived programs were assessed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and independently tested in frailty bulk-blood and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) whole-blood datasets. CellOracle simulations were used to prioritize candidate transcriptional regulators. Results Aging muscle showed increased inflammatory, extracellular-matrix, and stromal communication programs. During early AD-related brain progression, vascular and immune populations showed increasing inflammatory and matrix-associated activity together with shifts in intercellular communication. Cross-tissue analysis identified six concordantly enriched pathways comprising 109 leading-edge genes in endothelial populations and four pathways comprising 51 genes in myeloid populations. Related peripheral-blood signatures varied across cohorts and cell types. However, in independent frailty and ADNI mild cognitive impairment and AD datasets, 23 of 30 predefined tissue-derived pathway-subset tests showed significant positive enrichment after false-discovery-rate correction, whereas individual gene-level bulk-blood associations did not survive correction. CellOracle analyses prioritized ETS2 and BHLHE40 as exploratory endothelial regulators whose simulated perturbation consistently reduced selected shared program scores across tissues. Conclusions Aging skeletal muscle and AD-related brain tissue exhibit convergent endothelial and myeloid inflammatory programs, with related pathway-level signals detectable in peripheral blood. These cross-tissue programs and candidate endothelial regulators provide testable hypotheses for mechanisms linking systemic aging, muscle dysfunction, and AD-related neurodegeneration.
items.authors: Zhang, A.; Shen, W.; Yan, S.; Chen, J.; Liu, X.; Zou, J.; Li, S.; Hu, S.; Liu, Y.; Pan, C.; Lan, Z.; Peng, G.; Zhang, Q.; Peng, W.; Ahmadizar, F.; Zhang, J.

items.title: Bone regulates locomotion by sustaining motoneuronal mitochondrial function
items.abstract: Body-brain communication is crucial for optimal neuronal performance across the lifespan, yet whether peripheral organs regulate spinal cord motoneuron (MN) function through circulating molecules remains unknown. The expression of hormone receptors by spinal MNs raises the possibility that circulating cues allow the spinal cord to sense the body's energetic state and sustain motor activity. Here, we show that the bone-derived hormones osteocalcin (OCN) signals on spinal MNs via its receptor GPR158. GPR158 is selectively enriched in spinal cholinergic MNs, and its loss, globally or specifically in spinal MNs, or the one of OCN, impairs locomotor function and reduces choline acetyltransferase (ChAT) levels. Mechanistically, OCN signaling through GPR158 fine-tunes autophagy, mitophagy and mitochondrial activity in spinal MNs. Restoring any of these processes, by pharmacologically inducing mitophagy or chemogenetically activating mitochondria, is sufficient to rescue the locomotor deficits of Gpr158-deficient mice. Finally, OCN restoration in aged mice reverses age-related locomotor decline through a mechanism that requires MN autophagy and mitophagy. This study reveals that through OCN, the skeleton influences motor functions by fine-tuning motoneuronal mitochondria, and suggests that age-related motor decline is, at least in part, reversible.
items.authors: Romeo Guitart, D.; Tirani, T.; Milunov, D.; Torres-Juacida, A. K.; Lamotte, B.; Arenas-Plascencia, C.; Durand, S.; Nemazanyy, I.; Moriceau, S.; Saha, S.; Karsenty, G.; Oury, F.

items.title: Neural Evidence of Early Sensitivity to Text in Pre-reading Toddlers
items.abstract: Learning to read leads to widespread changes in brain organization, but it is not yet known when text first becomes a privileged stimulus. To test whether neural sensitivity to text can appear prior to reading instruction, 31 monolingual toddlers in Israel (2.1-3.6 years) not yet enrolled in school were presented with displays of real, native text and visually matched non-text symbols. Using functional near-infrared spectroscopy, we found different patterns of activity in response to text vs. non-text across multiple cortical regions. Most notably, text elicited more activity in the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex, a region often associated with language processing. These results suggest that through implicit sensitivity to regularities in their input, toddlers may be able to discover that text is a meaningful stimulus and could begin to develop associations that will allow them to build connections between language and text.
items.authors: Kherbawy, N.; Potter, C. E.; Jaffe-Dax, S.

items.title: The Effective Visual Acuity of Butterflies in Flight
items.abstract: The spatial visual acuity of an eye is determined by both the spatial sampling density of the retina and the angular sensitivity of individual photoreceptors. In insect compound eyes, these are respectively characterised by the interommatidial angle, {Delta}{varphi}, and photoreceptor acceptance angle, {Delta}{rho}. During movement, however, finite photoreceptor integration times cause retinal image motion to broaden the effective acceptance angle, potentially degrading spatial resolution beyond its anatomical limit. This problem is especially acute in flying insects, which experience large rotational velocities during locomotion and must actively stabilise gaze to limit retinal image motion. Butterflies present a particularly demanding case because their flight is characterised by large, wingbeat-coupled thoracic oscillations. Here, we quantify how gaze stabilisation limits motion blur in freely flying Monarch butterflies Danaus plexippus by combining free-flight kinematic reconstruction of the head and thorax with separate intracellular measurements of photoreceptor acceptance angles and integration times from quiescent butterflies. We found that, without head compensation, thoracic oscillations would broaden the effective photoreceptor acceptance angle from its quiescent value of 2.17{degrees} to 9.38{degrees} during take-off. Compensatory head movements substantially reduced this motion-induced broadening, limiting the effective acceptance angle to 5.28{degrees}. Nevertheless, this 2.4-fold broadening of effective photoreceptor acceptance angle represents a substantial degradation of spatial acuity in flight, highlighting motion blur as an important constraint on the visual ecology of flying butterflies.
items.authors: Supple, J. A.; Li, W.; Ilic, M.; Kos, M.; Lin, H.-T.; Belusic, G.; Krapp, H. G.

items.title: Reduction of complex dynamic touch information to a single stable perceptual feature
items.abstract: Dynamic touch requires the perceptual system to extract stable material properties from complex, evolving signals. Here, we examine potential material property features for a constrained dynamic-touch regime: brief taps, in which contact-induced vibratory transients are prominent and sustained deformation cues are reduced. Using a spectral-energy compensation method, we conducted five psychophysical experiments in two degraded-feedback scenarios: soft finger interfaces, in which fingertip stiffness was reduced by an inflatable silicone bubble, and compliant-surface interactions, in which participants tapped foam surfaces. Participants made explicit hardness judgments in two-alternative forced-choice tasks and identified rendered materials in multi-alternative matching and classification tasks. Under these tapping-based conditions, judgments scaled systematically with total spectral energy and were largely independent of waveform family. When spectral energy and dominant-frequency cues were placed in conflict, classifications predominantly followed spectral energy. These results identify total spectral energy as a robust cue for hardness judgments and material identification from brief taps, rather than as a complete account of hardness perception across all exploratory procedures. The findings provide a compact rendering principle for haptic interfaces in which contact-triggered vibrotactile feedback is available.
items.authors: Zamani, N.; Stephens-Fripp, B.; Tymms, C.; Chan, S.; Pardakhtim, R.; Culburtson, H.; Hartcher-O'Brien, J.

items.title: Voluntary engagement predicts recovery across rehabilitation time points after experimental spinal cord injury
items.abstract: Rehabilitation is the cornerstone of clinical care following spinal cord injury (SCI) and is frequently incorporated into preclinical studies to evaluate emerging therapies. However, the variables that influence the effectiveness of rehabilitation interventions in rodent models remain poorly characterized, limiting the translational value of preclinical research. Here, we performed a meta-analysis of 150 preclinical studies comprising more than 3000 rodents and 292 effect sizes to identify such factors associated with successful rehabilitation after SCI. Rehabilitation improved functional outcomes across multiple behavioral domains, with larger effects observed in thoracic than cervical injury models. Meta-regression identified environmental enrichment as the most effective strategy, particularly when combined with task-specific training. Longer rehabilitation duration was associated with improved recovery, whereas greater daily exposure to forced rehabilitation was associated with smaller gains. In contrast, prolonged access to voluntary rehabilitation did not show this relationship. Rehabilitation improved outcomes when initiated at all time points after injury, with greater benefits when initiated during the late subacute and intermediate phases. Rehabilitation approaches associated with higher stress burden produced reduced benefits, suggesting that stress may limit rehabilitation-induced recovery. Collectively, these findings identify rehabilitation type, duration, and delivery context as important determinants of recovery after SCI and support a broad therapeutic window for intervention. Our results favor low-stress, voluntary rehabilitation strategies that promote sustained engagement and provide principles for designing effective and biologically appropriate rehabilitation strategies, potentially improving translational success for emerging SCI therapies. One Sentence SummarySustained voluntary rehabilitation promotes functional recovery across stages of experimental spinal cord injury, whereas prolonged forced training may reduce its benefits.
items.authors: Griffin, J. M.; Papaioannou, P.; Menon, R.; Cheyne, O.; Kellaway, S.; Svirskis, D.; Jutzeler, C.; Aziz, A.; Bradke, F.

items.title: Intracranial electrophysiology reveals distinct neural representations of nociception and salience in the human brain
items.abstract: Neuroimaging studies have shown close overlap between neural representations of nociceptive stimuli and non-nociceptive, salient stimuli (such as low-probability sounds), leading to the proposal that nociception and salience share a common neural substrate in the human brain. Here we use high-resolution intracranial recordings from 13 neurosurgical patients (2,018 total electrodes) to show that neural representations of nociception and salience are anatomically and functionally distinct in the human brain. 77% of 107 electrodes that encoded nociceptive stimuli did not encode low-probability sounds ("nociceptive representations"), whereas 23% encoded both nociceptive and low-probability sounds ("salience representations"). Nociceptive representations were distinct from salience representations in terms of anatomical prevalence (posterior insula, inferior parietal, and perirolandic cortex vs. anterior insula, thalamus, and inferior frontal gyrus), timing (nociception preceded salience by 120 ms on a trial-by-trial basis), and function (intracranial electrical stimulation was more likely to cause sensory experience when applied near nociceptive representations, as compared to salience representations). These results provide strong evidence that nociception and salience have distinct neural substrates in the human brain, and that selective measurement of these distinct processes may help understand patient-to-patient variability in chronic pain and develop personalized brain stimulation treatments.
items.authors: Joshi, S.; Polat, M.; Pantis, S.; Garg, R.; Ahmed, S.; Huang, Y.; McGeoch, P. D.; Keller, C. J.; Buch, V. P.; Mackey, S.; Parvizi, J.; Ramayya, A. G.

items.title: Acceleration of vision changes object representations from infancy to adulthood
items.abstract: While much of the neural and cognitive machinery for visual perception is in place within weeks from birth, we identified and quantified a fundamental difference between infant and adult vision: the temporal rate at which meaningful visual information can be reliably extracted. Using frequency-tagging electroencephalography with rapid serial visual presentation, we found that object categorization at 4 and 9 months is respectively seven times and two to three times slower than in adults. Using quantitative information from infants experiments, we created and presented accelerated visual streams to adults, to match infants perceptual experience. We used deep convolutional neural networks to identify object representations that match those elicited in adults when accelerating the information flow. Results show that acceleration compromises finer-grained object distinction while sparing broad, general object representations. We propose that slow vision is a design feature of early development for preserving and highlighting the most stable and general features of the world.
items.authors: Spriet, C.; Serraille, E.; Naderi, S.; Agrebi, M.; Bouyahia, Z.; Derrode, S.; Kaiser, D.; Papeo, L.; Hochmann, J.-R.

items.title: Larger Pre-Speech Auditory Modulation Is Associated With Smaller Corrective Responses To Auditory Errors
items.abstract: PurposeDuring speech planning, the brain predicts the auditory consequences of its movements and modulates the auditory system--a process called pre-speech auditory modulation (PSAM). We investigated the link between PSAM and behavioral error correction and determined how aging influences these mechanisms. MethodsSeventeen young adults (18-32 years) and 13 older adults (50-85 years) performed a speaking task involving auditory feedback perturbations and a silent reading control. We measured electrophysiological responses (N1/P2) to auditory probes during speech planning and correlated these modulations with the magnitude of participants subsequent behavioral corrective responses. ResultsBoth groups showed significant modulation of N1 and P2. However, N1 modulation correlated with corrective responses only in young adults. Older adults showed reduced behavioral corrections and smaller, delayed P2 components. Despite these age-related behavioral differences and the loss of the modulation-correction correlation, older adults maintained modulation magnitudes comparable to those of younger adults. ConclusionsN1 modulation serves as a neural index of the brains predictive processes during speech planning. Aging appears to selectively disrupt the integration of these signals into motor output rather than the internal generation of the predictions themselves.
items.authors: Basciano, A.; Chao, S.-C.; Rogalsky, C.; Daliri, A.

items.title: Suicide notes as structured final communications
items.abstract: Humans often communicate meaningfully during existential transition, yet the structure of final communications before death remains poorly understood. Suicide notes provide rare behavioral records, but two questions remain unresolved: whether note-leavers represent the broader population of suicide decedents, and whether notes follow systematic narrative structures. We analyzed a nationwide police-investigated registry of 102,922 suicide deaths in South Korea from 2013 to 2020, including 38,044 notes. Note-leavers differed systematically from non-leavers across demographic, situational and behavioral characteristics, indicating that note production reflects a selective communicative act within the suicidal process. Modeling notes as sequential narratives, we identified consistent patterns across opening, middle and closing sections, organized around apology and shame, love and gratitude, and practical directives concerning post-mortem affairs. Emotional trajectories also varied by age and gender. These findings provide population-scale evidence that suicide notes are structured final communications shaped by social relationships and demographic context under extreme circumstances.
items.authors: Park, J. B.; Aderinwale, A. O.; Oh, S. Y.; Hur, Y. H.; Lee, S. J.; Kwon, S. W.; Jeong, J.

items.title: Assessment of Fairness and Bias of an Image-based Surgical Site Infection Detection AI Model
items.abstract: BackgroundEvaluating fairness in artificial intelligence (AI) is essential before clinical implementation to prevent unintended harm across diverse patient populations. This study assesses performance differences of an image-based surgical site infection (SSI) detection model across age, gender, geography, race, and skin color. MethodsModel development/validation study using retrospective, multicenter data across surgical subspecialties from adults who submitted an image of their incision via the electronic health record within 30 days of their procedure between 2019-2024. Area under receiver operating curve (AUROC) was compared by age ( 0.09), however geographical differences were significant: lowest AUROC 0.83 (95% CI 0.77-0.88) vs. highest AUROC 0.87 (95% CI 0.84-0.89, p=0.01). Temporal validation using 4,242 images from 1,353 patients between 2022-2023 showed intact fairness across subgroups ({Delta}AUROC [ ]0.06) except geography ({Delta}AUROC [ ]0.16). ConclusionsThe model behaved fairly across age, gender, race, and skin color, however geographical differences persisted. These findings have practical implications underscoring the importance of evaluating bias in clinical AI before deployment.
items.authors: Lee, F. G.; Choudhary, A.; Li-Han, L. Y.; Dale, E. L.; Bankes, A. C.; Varghese, C.; Anderson, S. S.; Habermann, E. B.; Etzioni, D. A.; McLaughlin, S. A.; Salehinejad, H.; Thiels, C. A.

items.title: A Framework for Analytical Validation of Genomic DNA-Based Shotgun Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing Workflows
items.abstract: Background Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) is increasingly adopted as a rapid and unbiased alternative to culture-based pathogen detection. However, standardized approaches for analytical validation of mNGS workflows are lacking. Validation strategies based solely on comparison with culture are inherently limited due to low diagnostic yield of culture, and the inability to derive analytical parameters such as limit of detection (LoD) from clinical samples with unknown microbial loads. Systematic analytical approaches are therefore required to define mNGS workflow performance independently of clinical comparators. In addition to diagnostics, mNGS is widely applied to microbiome profiling, where preservation of microbial diversity at low DNA inputs is a key performance criterion. Materials and Methods The analytical performance of the PaRTI-Seq mNGS workflow (Micronbrane, Taiwan), comprising host depletion, DNA extraction, library preparation, and bioinformatics analysis, was evaluated. Library-level analytical sensitivity was assessed using quantified genomic DNA (gDNA) from Enterobacter hormaechei, Candida albicans, and Mycobacterium smegmatis. Workflow-level sensitivity was evaluated using enumerated suspensions of E. hormaechei, Staphylococcus aureus, M. smegmatis, C. albicans and Aspergillus brasiliensis. Microbiome performance at low DNA input was evaluated using stool, saliva and gut mock community samples at 50ng, 5ng, and 0.5ng gDNA input and compared with an alternative low-input library preparation workflow. Results The library preparation module demonstrated analytical sensitivity down to 0.1 pg of E. hormaechei and C. albicans gDNA, and 1pg for M. smegmatis gDNA. Workflow-level LoDs were determined to be 1 CFU for E. hormaechei, 272 CFUs for S. aureus, 39 CFUs for A. brasiliensis, 36 CFUs for C. albicans and 3,702 CFUs for M. smegmatis. Differences in extraction efficiencies and extracted gDNA qualities appeared to be important determinants of workflow-level LoDs. For microbiome applications, Micronbrane Unison Ultra-low DNA input library preparation kit maintained more consistent bacterial diversity indices down to 5ng DNA input for stool and saliva samples, and the gut mock community than the comparator workflow. Conclusion This study outlines practical and generalizable analytical validation approaches for mNGS library preparation and complete workflows using defined spike-in models, providing a foundation for informed clinical interpretation and implementation of mNGS in diagnostic and microbiome applications.
items.authors: Chan, M. K. L.; Toh, K. Y.; Foo, K.; Saravanan, N.; Toh, T. S.; Lim, L.; Chionh, Y.-T.; Chang, J. H.; Wu, M.
items.title_zh: 基于基因组DNA的随机测序工作流分析验证框架
items.summary_zh: 背景：随机测序的宏基因组学（mNGS）作为一种快速且无偏见的病原体检测替代方法，正被越来越多地采用。然而，缺乏标准化的分析验证方法。仅基于与培养比较的验证策略存在固有限制，因培养的诊断产率低，且无法从未知微生物负荷的临床样本中推导分析参数如检测限（LoD）。因此，需要系统的分析方法独立定义mNGS工作流性能。mNGS不仅用于诊断，还广泛应用于微生物组分析，其中在低DNA输入下保持微生物多样性是关键性能标准。方法：评估了PaRTI-Seq mNGS工作流的分析性能，包括宿主去除、DNA提取、文库准备和生物信息学分析。使用来自不同微生物的定量基因组DNA评估文库级别的分析灵敏度，并通过枚举悬浮液评估工作流级别的灵敏度。
items.l1_lead: 研究提出了一种系统的分析验证框架，以评估随机测序宏基因组学工作流的性能，确保在低DNA输入下保持微生物多样性和提高检测灵敏度。
items.l2_summary:
随机测序的宏基因组学（mNGS）作为一种快速且无偏见的病原体检测方法，正逐渐被广泛应用。然而，目前在该领域缺乏标准化的分析验证方法，尤其是仅依赖与培养比较的验证策略存在固有限制。这是因为培养的诊断产率较低，且无法从未知微生物负荷的临床样本中推导出分析参数，如检测限（LoD）。因此，亟需一种系统的分析方法，以独立定义mNGS工作流的性能。

本研究评估了PaRTI-Seq mNGS工作流的分析性能，涵盖了宿主去除、DNA提取、文库准备和生物信息学分析等多个环节。研究中使用了来自不同微生物的定量基因组DNA，以评估文库级别的分析灵敏度，并通过枚举悬浮液来评估工作流级别的灵敏度。这种评估方法不仅关注mNGS在病原体检测中的应用，还考虑了其在微生物组分析中的广泛应用，特别是在低DNA输入情况下保持微生物多样性这一关键性能标准。

通过对PaRTI-Seq工作流的系统分析，研究为mNGS的应用提供了重要的性能验证框架，强调了在不同分析环节中保持高灵敏度的重要性。这一框架的建立将有助于推动mNGS在临床诊断和微生物组研究中的标准化应用，提升其在实际操作中的可靠性和有效性。

items.title: PD-RISK Index: Piloting an unsupervised toolkit to identify adults with Parkinson disease
items.abstract: Effective screening for Parkinson disease (PD) is important for symptom management and patient recruitment into disease-modifying trials. Here, we examined the performance of the PD-RISK Index toolkit in identifying PD patients at home without supervision. Between 2022-2024, we recruited 305 participants (ages, 40-85 years): 93 with typical PD; 66 had other neurological conditions; and 146 were healthy controls. Two versions of the toolkit were completed: An original, 69-item-long questionnaire with the 40-scent University-of-Pennsylvania-Smell-Identification-Test (UPSIT); thereafter, a simplified, 11-item-short questionnaire with a newly-developed 8-scent smell test and responses submitted online. The corresponding summary scores ('PD-RISK Indices') were calculated for each subject to evaluate diagnostic performances. In both versions, PD patients had higher questionnaire scores and worse olfaction than healthy controls (P<0.001), as expected; scores for subjects with other neurological conditions ranked at intermediate levels. The simplified 11-item questionnaire outperformed the original version in identifying PD. The abbreviated 8-scent smell test and the UPSIT booklet performed equally well in detecting hyposmia. The simplified PD-RISK Index showed the highest diagnostic performance in identifying PD patients amongst all participants; at a value of 23 (range, 0-100, where higher scores indicate higher PD risk), we measured a sensitivity of 0.98, specificity of 0.83, and positive and negative likelihood ratios of 5.88 and 0.02, respectively. The simplified 'PD-RISK Index' showed stable performance across sexes and disease duration. Our study reveals that unsupervised screening for manifest PD can be effectively carried out at home using an 11-item questionnaire, 8-scent smell test and online data entry.
items.authors: Li, J.; Grimes, K.; Saade, J.; Lewis, D.; Tomlinson, J. J.; Frank, A.; Ramsay, T.; Salmaso, N.; Manuel, D.; Schlossmacher, M. G.
items.title_zh: PD-RISK指数：无监督工具包识别帕金森病成人的初步研究
items.summary_zh: 有效筛查帕金森病（PD）对症状管理和患者招募至疾病修饰试验至关重要。本研究评估了PD-RISK指数工具包在无监督情况下识别PD患者的表现。2022年至2024年，我们招募了305名参与者（年龄40-85岁）：93名典型PD患者、66名其他神经系统疾病患者和146名健康对照者。工具包包括两个版本：原始的69项问卷和40嗅觉的宾夕法尼亚大学嗅觉识别测试（UPSIT），以及简化的11项问卷和新开发的8嗅觉测试，在线提交。结果显示，PD患者的问卷得分高于健康对照者，嗅觉更差（P<0.001），其他神经疾病患者得分居中。简化的11项问卷在识别PD方面优于原始版本，8嗅觉测试和UPSIT在检测嗅觉减退方面表现相当。简化的PD-RISK指数在所有参与者中识别PD患者的诊断性能最高。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，简化的PD-RISK指数工具包在无监督情况下有效识别帕金森病患者，诊断性能优于原始版本，且嗅觉测试结果显著区分PD患者与健康对照者。
items.l2_summary:
本研究旨在评估PD-RISK指数工具包在无监督情况下识别帕金森病（PD）患者的有效性，强调了有效筛查PD对症状管理和患者招募至疾病修饰试验的重要性。研究于2022年至2024年期间进行，共招募了305名参与者，年龄范围为40至85岁，其中包括93名典型PD患者、66名其他神经系统疾病患者和146名健康对照者。PD-RISK工具包包含两个版本：一个是原始的69项问卷和40项嗅觉的宾夕法尼亚大学嗅觉识别测试（UPSIT），另一个是简化的11项问卷和新开发的8项嗅觉测试，均可在线提交。

研究结果显示，PD患者在问卷得分上显著高于健康对照者，且嗅觉能力明显较差（P<0.001），而其他神经疾病患者的得分则介于两者之间。进一步分析发现，简化的11项问卷在识别PD方面的表现优于原始版本，且8项嗅觉测试与UPSIT在检测嗅觉减退方面的效果相当。最终，简化的PD-RISK指数在所有参与者中识别PD患者的诊断性能最高。这些结果表明，PD-RISK指数工具包，尤其是其简化版本，能够有效识别PD患者，为未来的临床应用和研究提供了有力支持。

items.title: Biological network identifies pathways linking mental health drugs to adverse weight-related side effects
